text:
The search found related mechanisms, but no verified 2023–2026 NextItNet extension directly establishing input-dependent context resets. [FADC (CVPR 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05369) adjusts dilation per spatial position using local frequency information; useful architectural inspiration, with evidence from vision rather than recommendation. [DyS4Rec (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2025.107134) learns to skip irrelevant historical interactions in sequential recommendation. [Mamba (2023/2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.00752) demonstrates input-dependent propagation and forgetting, offering a selection principle transferable as a hypothesis without replacing NextItNet’s convolutional backbone.

Proposed adaptation: gate individual causal convolution taps using the current prefix representation and the corresponding historical feature, before summation. This selects information within each receptive field rather than merely weighting fixed-depth outputs. A stronger reset variant could attenuate a tap by the product of learned retention gates across intervening positions, suppressing paths crossing inferred context boundaries. Both are proposed mechanisms, not established results from these papers; retain causal inputs, padding masks, residual connections, and one jointly trained network per category.

Controls should compare against parameter-matched ungated convolutions, uniform gates, learned input-independent tap weights, and fixed recent-history windows. Shuffle gates across examples or replace them with their means to test whether input dependence matters. Evaluate older-history removal separately from corruption: stronger sensitivity to recent perturbations establishes reliance, not harm from older context. Report macro validation HR@10 alongside gate variability, effective lag usage, and results by history length; keep seeds, training budget, and candidate sets fixed.
